overview: The Middle Kingdom was a renewed phase of Egyptian political unity, beginning with Mentuhotep II’s reunification. Its art and institutions changed across Dynasties 11-13; the Met dates the phase approximately 2030-1650 BCE.

items.text: Early Dynasty 12 rulers established a northern capital at Itjtawi. Royal sponsorship of provincial temples linked kingship with regional religious centers.
Portraits of Senwosret III and Amenemhat III used mature faces. Their precise relationship to changing concepts of kingship remains interpretive.
Elite jewelry combined minute inlays with carefully decorated backs, demonstrating labor invested even in details hidden during use.
Private memorials at sacred centers depicted extended families and associates. Some tombs also accommodated multiple people.
Dynasty 13 saw many short reigns. Evidence does not establish a formal system of rotating ceremonial kings, and the period’s endpoint is approximate.

sources.title: Adela Oppenheim, Met, Egypt in the Middle Kingdom
sources.note: Checked passages and chronology qualifications appear in the accompanying evidence dossier.
